items.title: Shopping bag line shows "Added on" with today's date after adding a product
covers: AC1: line says 'Added on' and the date
Implementation Notes: format d MMM yyyy under the product name
items.reason: AC1 is the user-visible outcome of the story: without it the stored date is invisible. Only the e2e layer exercises the whole path (WebApp add → Basket gRPC → Redis → GetBasket → CartPage rendering and date format).

items.title: Changing a line's quantity in the shopping bag keeps its "Added on" date
covers: AC2: change quantity, date does not change
items.reason: AC2: the bag's quantity update sends the whole basket back, which could overwrite or drop the date. The e2e run proves the WebApp update path keeps the line's date shown; the day-level proof (date stays on an earlier day) is TC-ADDED-1-06.

items.title: Adding more of a product already in the bag keeps its "Added on" date
covers: AC2: add more of it, date does not change
items.reason: AC2 names "add more of it" separately from changing the quantity; it goes through the product page's add flow rather than the bag's update, so it is a separate path that could reset the date.

items.title: Removing a product and adding it again shows it with today's date
covers: AC3: removed and added again shows the date it was added again
items.reason: AC3 through the real UI: removal and a fresh add must produce a line that again carries a date (not none, not a lost one). Within one test run the old and new dates are the same day, so the "later day" proof is the unit case TC-ADDED-1-08.

items.title: UpdateBasket stamps a newly added product with the current UTC time
covers: AC4: API keeps the time a product was first added
Implementation Notes: product id not in the stored basket gets the current UTC time
items.reason: The first-added time must come from the server clock at the moment of the first add; a wrong or missing stamp breaks AC1. Unit layer with a fake `TimeProvider` gives an exact, deterministic time.

items.title: UpdateBasket keeps the stored added_at when the quantity changes days later
covers: AC2: change quantity, date does not change
Implementation Notes: keep each product's existing added_at
items.reason: AC2's core rule. `UpdateBasket` replaces the whole basket, so without reading the stored value the date would reset to "now". The fake clock lets the update happen on a later day, which an e2e run cannot.

items.title: UpdateBasket ignores an added_at sent by the client
covers: AC2: date does not change
AC4: API keeps the time a product was first added
Implementation Notes: the client's own value is never trusted
items.reason: `added_at` is on the request message too, so a client (or a stale WebApp copy) could overwrite the first-added time, which would break AC2 and AC4. Unit layer because only the gRPC service mapping decides this.

items.title: A product removed and added again later gets the time of the new add
covers: AC3: removed and added again later gets the new date
items.reason: AC3: after a removal the old date must not come back. Two sequential updates on different days against a repository substitute that keeps the last saved basket prove the removed line's time is forgotten.

items.title: GetBasket returns each line's stored added_at
covers: AC4: returns it with the basket
Implementation Notes: GetBasket returns the stored value
items.reason: The WebApp reads the date only from `GetBasket`; if it is not mapped to the response, AC1 shows nothing. Unit layer checks the exact mapping without Redis.

items.title: GetBasket returns a line stored without a date with no added_at
covers: AC4: a basket stored before this change still loads; its lines show no date
items.reason: AC4 requires old baskets to keep working; a line without a stored time must not fail the call nor get an invented date (for example 1970-01-01 or now), which the bag would then display.

items.title: A line stored without a date stays without one when its quantity changes
covers: AC4: its lines show no date until they are added again
AC2: date does not change
items.reason: AC4 says an old line shows no date "until added again"; a quantity change is not an add (AC2), so stamping it with "now" would show a wrong date. This is the edge between the "existing product" and "new product" rules.

items.title: Redis repository loads a basket JSON stored before the change
covers: AC4: a basket stored before this change still loads
items.reason: Old baskets live in Redis as JSON without an `AddedAt` property; deserialization with the source-generated context must accept it. Only a real Redis (the `Basket.FunctionalTests` `RedisFixture`) proves the stored bytes load.

items.title: Redis repository persists and returns AddedAt exactly
covers: AC4: the Basket API keeps the time a product was first added for every line
items.reason: AC4 "keeps the time": the value must survive serialization to Redis and back with its instant and UTC kind intact, or later reads show a shifted date. Needs real Redis.

subject: ADDED-1
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 8/10, sol 7/10; 6 finding(s) stand, 0 note(s).

items.reason: Upheld finding sol-1 (AC3) requires a deterministic regression test: an UpdateBasket that read the stored basket before a concurrent remove and re-add of a product must not write back the old AddedAt. The plan has no such case, and its Open questions wrongly say the story is silent. Add a unit case tagged kept-for: sol-1. The repository substitute's UpdateBasketAsync calls the update function, then a concurrent write removes product 99 and re-adds it with AddedAt 2026-11-20T10:00:00Z, then it calls the function again on the new stored basket. Expected: the saved and returned product 99 has AddedAt 2026-11-20T10:00:00Z, not the original 2026-11-01T09:00:00Z. Optionally add the functional counterpart against real Redis (a conditional update retries against a basket written between its read and its write).

Upheld findings sol-3 and opus-r2-1 require UpdateBasket to report repeated concurrent-write conflicts as StatusCode.Aborted, not NotFound, and ask for deterministic coverage. The plan says 'No case asserts that outcome'. Add a case tagged kept-for: sol-3. Unit: the repository's UpdateBasketAsync throws BasketConcurrencyException. Expected: RpcException with StatusCode.Aborted, not NotFound. Functional: against real Redis, every conditional write conflicts, and after 10 attempts the call throws BasketConcurrencyException.

items.file: _index.md: Open questions; upheld review finding sol-1
items.reason: The index excludes concurrency, but upheld finding sol-1 explicitly requires deterministic regression coverage. Add a case interleaving a paused quantity update with removal and re-addition, then verify the final persisted and returned timestamp is the re-addition timestamp; also cover competing first additions preserving the first committed timestamp.

items.file: _index.md: Open questions; upheld review findings sol-3 and opus-r2-1
items.reason: Upheld finding sol-3 requires deterministic retry-exhaustion coverage and its service response. Add a case forcing every conditional write to conflict, asserting the selected concurrency status (Aborted for the described implementation), rather than NotFound, and confirming the conflicting stored basket is not overwritten.

AC4 requires legacy lines to show no date. API null-field assertions cannot detect the WebApp rendering a default date or an empty 'Added on' label. Add an e2e case that seeds an undated Redis line for alice, opens /cart, and asserts the product remains visible with no 'Added on' text.

Both functional cases invoke repository methods directly instead of naming an API request, status and response as required by Project context. Retain direct Redis setup where needed, but exercise Basket gRPC through the functional host: GetBasket must return OK with absent added_at for legacy JSON; UpdateBasket followed by GetBasket must return OK with the persisted server-assigned timestamp.

subject: test-planner
reason: The UI journeys (AC1–AC3) and an undated old line (AC4) are e2e cases. Clock and timestamp rules plus the concurrency regressions for sol-1/sol-3 are unit cases with a fake TimeProvider and a substitute repository that runs the update twice. Redis storage, old JSON, the conditional retry and retry exhaustion are functional cases: through gRPC where the API contract is checked, and at repository level where a write has to be injected mid-update.

items.reason: Upheld finding sol-1: a quantity update that read the stored basket, then lost the race to a remove + re-add of the same product, must not write the stale first-added time back, or AC3's "date is the day I added it again" breaks. The unit layer drives the interleaving deterministically by making the repository substitute call the service's update function twice, as the real conditional write does on conflict.

covers: AC4: keeps the time a product was first added
AC2: add more of it, date does not change
Implementation Notes: product id not in the stored basket gets the current UTC time
items.reason: Upheld finding sol-1 also names competing first additions: two requests that both saw no product 99 must not let the later one overwrite the time the earlier one committed, or the "first added" time moves forward (AC4, AC2). The unit layer makes the race deterministic with a repository substitute that calls the update function again after a concurrent write.

items.title: The Redis conditional update retries against a basket written between its read and its write
covers: AC3: removed and added again gets the date it was added again
Implementation Notes: optimistic Redis transaction re-reads and recomputes on conflict
items.reason: Upheld finding sol-1: the protection in TC-ADDED-1-14 only holds if the real Redis transaction actually detects a write made between its read and its write and re-runs the update on the new value. A substitute cannot prove the Redis condition; only real Redis can. The concurrent write must land inside the update function, so this case calls `RedisBasketRepository.UpdateBasketAsync(buyerId, update)` directly rather than through gRPC.

items.title: UpdateBasket reports repeated concurrent-write conflicts as Aborted, not NotFound
covers: AC3: a stale timestamp is never written
Implementation Notes: retries exhausted after concurrent writes
items.reason: Upheld findings sol-3 and opus-r2-1: when the repository gives up after repeated conflicts, the service must tell the client the update was aborted and can be retried; reporting `NotFound` ("basket does not exist") is false and hides the conflict. Only the gRPC service decides the status, so the unit layer with a throwing substitute pins it exactly.

items.title: The Redis conditional update gives up after 10 conflicting attempts and leaves the concurrent basket in place
covers: AC3: a stale timestamp is never written
Implementation Notes: up to 10 attempts, then the update is abandoned

items.title: Changing a line's quantity in the shopping bag keeps its "Added on" date
covers: AC2: change quantity, date does not change
items.reason: AC2: the bag's quantity update sends the whole basket back, which could overwrite or drop the date. The e2e run proves the WebApp update path keeps the line's date shown; the day-level proof (date stays on an earlier day) is TC-ADDED-1-06.

items.title: Adding more of a product already in the bag keeps its "Added on" date
covers: AC2: add more of it, date does not change

items.title: Removing a product and adding it again shows it with today's date
covers: AC3: removed and added again shows the date it was added again
items.reason: AC3 through the real UI: removal and a fresh add must produce a line that again carries a date (not none, not a lost one). Within one test run the old and new dates are the same day, so the "later day" proof is the unit case TC-ADDED-1-08.

items.title: UpdateBasket stamps a newly added product with the current UTC time
covers: AC4: API keeps the time a product was first added
Implementation Notes: product id not in the stored basket gets the current UTC time
items.reason: The first-added time must come from the server clock at the moment of the first add; a wrong or missing stamp breaks AC1. Unit layer with a fake `TimeProvider` gives an exact, deterministic time.

items.title: UpdateBasket keeps the stored added_at when the quantity changes days later
covers: AC2: change quantity, date does not change
Implementation Notes: keep each product's existing added_at
items.reason: AC2's core rule. `UpdateBasket` replaces the whole basket, so without reading the stored value the date would reset to "now". The fake clock lets the update happen on a later day, which an e2e run cannot.

items.title: UpdateBasket ignores an added_at sent by the client
covers: AC2: date does not change
AC4: API keeps the time a product was first added
Implementation Notes: the client's own value is never trusted
items.reason: `added_at` is on the request message too, so a client (or a stale WebApp copy) could overwrite the first-added time, which would break AC2 and AC4. Unit layer because only the gRPC service mapping decides this.

items.title: A product removed and added again later gets the time of the new add
covers: AC3: removed and added again later gets the new date

items.title: Shopping bag line shows "Added on" with today's date after adding a product
covers: AC1: line says 'Added on' and the date
Implementation Notes: format d MMM yyyy under the product name
items.reason: AC1 is the user-visible outcome of the story: without it the stored date is invisible. Only the e2e layer exercises the whole path (WebApp add → Basket gRPC → Redis → GetBasket → CartPage rendering and date format).

items.title: Changing a line's quantity in the shopping bag keeps its "Added on" date
covers: AC2: change quantity, date does not change
items.reason: AC2: the bag's quantity update sends the whole basket back, which could overwrite or drop the date. The e2e run proves the WebApp update path keeps the line's date shown; the day-level proof (date stays on an earlier day) is TC-ADDED-1-06.

items.title: Adding more of a product already in the bag keeps its "Added on" date
covers: AC2: add more of it, date does not change
items.reason: AC2 names "add more of it" separately from changing the quantity; it goes through the product page's add flow rather than the bag's update, so it is a separate path that could reset the date.

items.title: Removing a product and adding it again shows it with today's date
covers: AC3: removed and added again shows the date it was added again
items.reason: AC3 through the real UI: removal and a fresh add must produce a line that again carries a date (not none, not a lost one). Within one test run the old and new dates are the same day, so the "later day" proof is the unit case TC-ADDED-1-08.

items.title: UpdateBasket stamps a newly added product with the current UTC time
covers: AC4: API keeps the time a product was first added
Implementation Notes: product id not in the stored basket gets the current UTC time
items.reason: The first-added time must come from the server clock at the moment of the first add; a wrong or missing stamp breaks AC1. Unit layer with a fake `TimeProvider` gives an exact, deterministic time.

items.title: UpdateBasket keeps the stored added_at when the quantity changes days later
covers: AC2: change quantity, date does not change
Implementation Notes: keep each product's existing added_at
items.reason: AC2's core rule. `UpdateBasket` replaces the whole basket, so without reading the stored value the date would reset to "now". The fake clock lets the update happen on a later day, which an e2e run cannot.

items.title: UpdateBasket ignores an added_at sent by the client
covers: AC2: date does not change
AC4: API keeps the time a product was first added
Implementation Notes: the client's own value is never trusted
items.reason: `added_at` is on the request message too, so a client (or a stale WebApp copy) could overwrite the first-added time, which would break AC2 and AC4. Unit layer because only the gRPC service mapping decides this.

items.title: A product removed and added again later gets the time of the new add
covers: AC3: removed and added again later gets the new date
items.reason: AC3: after a removal the old date must not come back. Two sequential updates on different days against a repository substitute that keeps the last saved basket prove the removed line's time is forgotten.

items.title: GetBasket returns a line stored without a date with no added_at
covers: AC4: a basket stored before this change still loads; its lines show no date
AC4: returns it with the basket
Implementation Notes: GetBasket returns the stored value
items.reason: AC4 requires old baskets to keep working; a line without a stored time must not fail the call nor get an invented date (for example 1970-01-01 or now), which the bag would then display.

items.title: A line stored without a date stays without one when its quantity changes
covers: AC4: its lines show no date until they are added again
AC2: date does not change
items.reason: AC4 says an old line shows no date "until added again"; a quantity change is not an add (AC2), so stamping it with "now" would show a wrong date. This is the edge between the "existing product" and "new product" rules.

items.title: GetBasket over gRPC loads a basket JSON stored before the change and returns no added_at
covers: AC4: a basket stored before this change still loads
AC4: its lines show no date
Implementation Notes: GetBasket returns none for a line stored without one
items.reason: Old baskets live in Redis as JSON without an `AddedAt` property. The source-generated deserializer and the gRPC mapping must both accept that and return the line with no `added_at`. Only the Basket API host running against a real Redis proves the stored bytes load through the real `GetBasket` call; the unit case TC-ADDED-1-10 mocks the repository.

items.title: UpdateBasket over gRPC persists the server-assigned added_at and GetBasket returns it exactly
covers: AC4: the Basket API keeps the time a product was first added for every line and returns it with the basket
items.reason: AC4 "keeps the time ... and returns it": the server-assigned time must survive the gRPC mapping, serialization to Redis and back with its instant intact, or later reads show a shifted or missing date. Needs the Basket API host against a real Redis; the unit cases mock the repository.

items.title: A quantity update that read the basket before a concurrent remove and re-add does not write back the old date
covers: AC3: removed and added again gets the date it was added again
AC2: date does not change
Implementation Notes: UpdateBasket recomputes AddedAt on a conflicting write
items.reason: Upheld finding sol-1: a quantity update that read the stored basket, then lost the race to a remove + re-add of the same product, must not write the stale first-added time back, or AC3's "date is the day I added it again" breaks. The unit layer drives the interleaving deterministically by making the repository substitute call the service's update function twice, as the real conditional write does on conflict.

items.title: Of two competing first adds of a product, the first committed time is kept
covers: AC4: keeps the time a product was first added
AC2: add more of it, date does not change
Implementation Notes: product id not in the stored basket gets the current UTC time
items.reason: Upheld finding sol-1 also names competing first additions: two requests that both saw no product 99 must not let the later one overwrite the time the earlier one committed, or the "first added" time moves forward (AC4, AC2). The unit layer makes the race deterministic with a repository substitute that calls the update function again after a concurrent write.

items.title: The Redis conditional update retries against a basket written between its read and its write
covers: AC3: removed and added again gets the date it was added again
Implementation Notes: optimistic Redis transaction re-reads and recomputes on conflict
items.reason: Upheld finding sol-1: the protection in TC-ADDED-1-14 only holds if the real Redis transaction detects a write made between its read and its write and re-runs the service's update on the new value. A substitute cannot prove the Redis condition; only real Redis behind the hosted gRPC service can. The concurrent write is placed deterministically inside the update by a test repository wrapper registered in the host, so the case exercises `UpdateBasket` and `GetBasket` over gRPC rather than calling the repository directly.

items.title: UpdateBasket reports repeated concurrent-write conflicts as Aborted, not NotFound
covers: AC3: a stale timestamp is never written
Implementation Notes: retries exhausted after concurrent writes
items.reason: Upheld findings sol-3 and opus-r2-1: when the repository gives up after repeated conflicts, the service must tell the client the update was aborted and can be retried; reporting `NotFound` ("basket does not exist") is false and hides the conflict. Only the gRPC service decides the status, so the unit layer with a throwing substitute pins it exactly.

items.title: The Redis conditional update gives up after 10 conflicting attempts and leaves the concurrent basket in place
covers: AC3: a stale timestamp is never written
Implementation Notes: up to 10 attempts, then the update is abandoned
items.reason: Upheld finding sol-3: retry exhaustion must end in `BasketConcurrencyException`, reported to the gRPC caller as `Aborted`, and must not fall back to an unconditional write that overwrites the competing basket with stale data. Only real Redis behind the hosted gRPC service proves the condition fails on every attempt, that nothing is written and what status the client sees; a test repository wrapper in the host makes every attempt conflict deterministically.

items.title: A shopping bag line stored before the change shows no "Added on" text
covers: AC4: a basket stored before this change still loads; its lines show no date
Implementation Notes: nothing for a line without a date
items.reason: AC4 says old lines "show no date". The API cases (TC-ADDED-1-10, TC-ADDED-1-12) prove `added_at` is absent, but cannot detect the WebApp rendering a default date (for example `Added on 1 Jan 0001`) or an empty "Added on" label. Only the e2e layer checks what the shopper sees. The scenarios seed Postgres only, so the spec writes the legacy Redis value itself.
